actions.action: Free replacement card on request and payment alerts
Instant dispute credit up to $100 per customer, 8 weeks

message: Update on the card charges from Nov 16-17: our card processor confirmed a fault that charged some payments twice, and a small number of cards had fraud test charges of $0.50 to $2 after card numbers were stolen elsewhere, for example on a fake shopping site. Cobalt's own systems were not breached. About 9,000 customers were affected. Starting today, for 8 weeks: if you dispute a card charge, we credit up to $100 right away while we investigate. In the app you can turn on an alert for every card payment and order a free new card.
why: The week-4 facts are far smaller than the 'Cobalt got hacked' rumor, but many customers only heard the rumor.
Instant dispute credit and payment alerts give every customer a concrete way to protect themselves before the migration.
We repeat only what the processor confirmed and promise nothing about refunds we cannot yet confirm.

target: paycheck customers who work for the federal government or its contractors
message: If your pay is delayed by the government shutdown because you work for the federal government or a federal contractor, you can get a zero-interest advance of up to $500 from Cobalt. No fees and no interest; it is repaid from your next paycheck deposit. Request it in the app under Pay. We will tell you as soon as we know more.
why: The shutdown leaves some paycheck customers with no pay date before Christmas bills.
A zero-interest advance up to $500 covers the gap for about the number of customers affected.
It costs $0.4M and is repaid from their next deposit, so we help without buying loyalty.
